name: Projects
description: An (incomplete) list of past and present projects I've worked on. Some are big, some are small, some are done, some active, some in-between. I've organised them as a graph you can step through; feel free to explore. Almost all projects contain some URL to click on.

name: Social Projects
description: Some projects related to bringing people together.

name: Programming
description: All my projects that mostly consist of programming. With AI coding, many of these projects could be completed much, much quicker than when I worked on them. I find that a little sad, but I also realise that all of these projects are already in the context of the time of creation and my current set of skills.

name: Terminal Website
description: My terminal website, serving as my homepage. Over 200 commands, home to many more smaller projects. There are A LOT of fun games to play, secrets to find, simulations to run and tools to use.

name: Maths
description: I started liking Mathematics as a fun thing to do in school and have since made many projects to communicate, teach, research and illustrate some maths. I studied/study Mathematics at Trinity College Dublin and ETH Zürich for my Bachelor's.

name: Social Media Accounts
description: I have (public) accounts on various Social Media platforms.

name: YouTube
description: My YouTube channel where I sometimes make videos about things I want to talk about, which are often related to Maths and/or Programming.

name: Hackathons
description: I like to participate in Hackathons. I won once in Dublin at HackTrinity in 2023, which was also my very first Hackathon. I think Hackathons have suffered a lot from AI. I've mostly participated in Dublin, including at HackTrinity, HackIreland and HackEurope (the Trilogy (Trinity)).

name: Recreational Maths Zürich
description: I started 'Recreational Maths Zürich' in the spring semester 2025. It's a club about promoting and supporting recreational maths projects for students in Zürich. Right now (October '26) it has over 300 members and has organised over 40 weekly meetups. I still run it as president, but wouldn't mind if someone else would like to take over.

name: Mathathon 2026
description: Recmaths organised a competition where 100 students coded algorithms to play games against each other live overnight. There were hourly live tournaments on a big board, side events, catering and free drinks and many great moments. It went really well and it hopefully wasn't the last one (it was the second one we organised). It was hosted in collaboration with Mind:Phair (an association of VMP at ETH Zürich).

name: Android Apps
description: I've made some Android Apps over the years. Most of my Apps were hosted on the Google Play Store. Unfortunately, Google decided to close my developer account, removing all my apps (I paid for the account, grr!). I have since opened a new account (which costs money, again!) but am not planning on re-adding my old apps, mostly because they really weren't that great.

name: Perli
description: Perli was an app to train your memory, based off the idea that you saw some bombs in a small grid (e.g. 5x5), then had to memorize these bomb positions and then had to draw a path from a random starting point to a random end point without touching any of the bombs (naturally, the bombs were hidden for this part of the game). The app contained a great music soundtrack and sound effects made by my friend Mattis Strickert and many levels of varying difficulty. It even contained custom buyable grid-skins and a one-minute challenge mode. Looking back at it, it was a really fun app!

name: Library of Léon
description: I read Jorge Luis Borges' short story on 'The Library of Babel' and wanted to recreate the Library in a cool 3d-way, while also extending it to contain all possible texts. Basically, it's a 3d library where each floor contains all possible texts ('books'). In the short story, these are all distributed randomly. There are a lot of weird things to realise about this concept. For example, there must be one book somewhere containing the answer to any question anyone has ever asked. In fact, even this very text is in the library (see the link below). I'm really proud of the resulting website and Maths behind it; there are a lot of fun things about it. I also made a YouTube video about it. Oh and I added a terrifying Horror Game to it. The website (the Library of Léon (lol)) is inspired by Jonathan Basile's great implementation of the Library of Babel as described in the short story.

name: Paper Packing
description: In October 2025, I realised that the Standard for A4 paper defines it in whole millimetres. I subsequently realised that the resulting error means that you can fit more sheets of A10 into one A0 than you 'should'. I proved exactly how many actually fit in (surprisingly difficult mathematical question, see research paper I presented at the FUN26 conference), made a YouTube video about it, got it featured on Matt Parker's YouTube channel and am still working on it some more. There are still some questions left unanswered that I would like to answer.

name: AntiCookieBox
description: A chrome plugin to remove popups asking for cookie approval. It was always a bit wonky, but nowadays it's even more wonky. It doesn't really work, but apparently some people liked it, given it had over 300 users. It was one of my first major programming projects. It got removed recently because of the Manifest V3 Update.

name: Stray
description: A flutter app that lets you hunt virtual coins in the real world. Here is the (oh god how embarrassing) text from the Google Play page (that's now gone): 'Embark on an exciting urban adventure with our innovative treasure hunt app! Discover the thrill of chasing goals as you explore your city like never before. With just a tap, generate a coin placed randomly between 1 and 5 kilometers away from your location. Armed only with a compass pointing you in a direction, set off on a captivating quest to find the hidden treasure.'

name: Partycolo
description: At the end of high school, I was frustrated with paid drinking game apps. So I made my own! It's very embarrassing and the questions came from some random websites I found. Oh and it's in German.

name: HR-Codes (Hackathon Project)
description: A new standard for QR Codes! These codes are not just computer-readable, but also human-readable (aren't they all, you may say now)! Isn't that awesome?! My team and I made this overnight and won the Hackathon (HackTrinity 2023 at Trinity College Dublin).

name: 3d Homepage
description: I decided that 3d websites would be the future and made a home-world that you can enter and interact with. It's not very big nor complex, but I still think it's kind of cool.

name: Turtlo
description: There's this fun command on the terminal website that spawns a turtle following your cursor (turtlo) and playing around. Because it's so awesome, I made a chrome plugin which spawns it on every site you visit. I turned it off on my machine because it's so annoying.

name: Covid in Coville
description: Covid in Coville was a project done for a German national science fair when I was in high school in 2022. I won the Lower Saxony regional and state competition in the 'Computer Science / Maths' category. I won some prizes on the national level, including a scholarship at a university of the German military and the Konrad-Zuse Youth-Prize for Computer Science given out by the Eduard-Rhein-Foundation. It was about simulating the spread of a city in an interactive web-app. The project materials are in German only.

links.name: Local News Article about it (Braunschweiger Zeitung)

name: Compli
description: My first Android App! It was a shitty app that shows the time since you last gave a compliment - thus making you want to give more compliments to people in your life! It doesn't work anymore; it was built with Android Studio.

name: Projects Page
description: Well, it's this website! Collecting all of these projects and writing them all down including links and dating is surprisingly difficult.

name: Spion
description: A game I made with a friend that you play by passing your phone around. Description from the website: 'Each player is assigned a role: spy or agent. The agents must find out who the spy is. The spy must find out where they are. To do this, the players ask each other questions. The spy must try to answer the questions without revealing their location. The agents must try to find out who is a spy without giving too obvious a clue as to their location. The agents win if they have unmasked all the spies. A player can be unmasked by asking if they are a spy. If an agent is accidentally unmasked, the spies win. The spy wins if they find out where they are. They can say at any time 'I am a spy and I know where I am.' Then they must say where they are. If they guess correctly, the spies win.'

name: Selfmade Productivity Things
description: I'm not a fan of MS Office or the Google Office suite apps. So I made a few of my own web-based apps that do some stuff that Todo apps, Word and Powerpoint do.

name: Lettre
description: A bad text editor on the web that you can use to write texts. On the website I wrote that it was made to be 'less distracting'. In modern language: I didn't know how to implement complex things. I once wrote a Poetry Slam text for my German class in high school using this website. On the day of the Slam, I opened the site and the text somehow got lost (with no backups). It was very hard to explain to the teacher what happened. Needless to say, they didn't really believe me and instead assumed that I forgot to do it. I had to improvise the text in the class itself and it actually turned out to be quite good (the substitute spontaneous text). I'd love to do some Poetry Slam in the future; it seems like a fun idea! Anyhow, all of this is to say that you should maybe not use this app for real-life things, even though I still think it has a nice aesthetic.

name: Presi
description: Bad presentation software to use instead of Google Sheets or Powerpoint. I actually used it for a couple of presentations in school and enjoyed it a lot. I wouldn't trust the autosave too much, but I think it's still kind of cool!

name: Todo
description: A crappy todo app without any security. It does what it wants to kind of well. I know some people still use it to this day; it works okay. It's nice that it's easily accessible even across devices. On the bad side, this also means that it's very accessible for other people to access your todos, which might be very personal. Please don't trust this site too much.

name: Satisfying Clicks
description: A chrome plugin that spawns click effects every time you click anywhere on your screen on any website you visit. It has surprisingly many users.

name: FeelBadTimer
description: An app that constantly shows a floating timer on your screen showing how much time you've spent on your phone already. It's supposed to make you feel bad, hence the name. It's not publicly released yet, but it should be released soon (Written in October 2026).

links.name: Play Store Page (might not be public yet)

name: QR Code Projects
description: I've been obsessed with QR codes for a while now. I think the concept is really cool. I'm especially interested in the computer-human interaction they embody. I love the fact that you can learn to read them by hand (and even draw them by hand!). I've made a few projects related to this.

name: HQR Codes
description: A website to generate QR codes that contain some text on them. They put the text on top not just by abusing error correction, but also by changing QR parameters like the padding data to make the text appear. Isn't that cool?

name: QR Studio
description: An interactive QR code drawing tool that lets you draw them step-by-step.

name: Draw on QR Codes
description: A site that lets you create QR codes that contain some content while also preserving something you drew on them. It uses all the tricks!

name: Read QR by hand
description: A worksheet to learn to read QR Codes by hand.

name: World-Cup Prediction
description: I made a simple mathematical model to predict the knockout phase of the 2026 FIFA World Cup. It might not be very accurate, but it's good at giving an intuition for counter-intuitive tournament probabilities.

name: @everyone
description: From the GitHub Repo description: '@everyone is a rapid-contact web app designed for urgent personal situations (mental health crises, safety check-ins, and similar moments where reaching someone fast matters).' I developed it with three others at HackEurope 2026. It was a great time, but we didn't score well. It was basically a button to press in case of panic attacks that calls all of your friends at the same time and connects you to the one picking up first. I still like the idea a lot.

name: Tabletop
description: Have you ever wanted to play cards with friends but forgotten to bring the actual cards? No worries! This is the website for you. One person opens the website on their tv/computer; the others connect to it via WebRTC and they can interact and play any card game just by dragging the cards. It has a couple of useful features. I spent quite a while on this. It's a shame I've never used it. It's just worse than playing cards in real life. Perhaps this will be useful in the next epidemic.

name: Dynamic Systems
description: I took a course on dynamic systems and decided to make them into interactive fun things to play with on my website. I implemented the doubling map, the baker map and the cat map.

name: Zürich Tram Travelling Salesman
description: I wanted to visit all Tram Stations in Zürich in one day, only by Tram. Using public timetables, I tried to find optimized paths using different approaches such as Time-Dependent Ant Colony Optimization, Heuristic-Optimized Nearest-Neighbour Searches and more. This problem is a Time-Dependent Travelling-Salesperson-Problem (TD-TSP) and is significantly harder than the 'traditional' TSP, as the introduction of timetables makes 'traditional' efficient optimization techniques hard. Since I want paths that are executable in real life, the optimization also includes minimum buffer times and plan-B optimizations. I actually did it and set the new record of 9h 35min.

name: Williampedia
description: An AI agent going rogue and writing his own wiki. You could see what articles he wrote and there was even a Twitch livestream where you could watch him work tirelessly. It got pretty complicated, and it was quite cool. We worked on it at the HackIreland Hackathon in 2025. I liked it, but it also didn't score very well. In retrospect, it's quite similar to Grokipedia, only that it doesn't actually pretend that it's an actually usable Wiki (which is quite the important distinction in my opinion).

name: multi.golf
description: An online minigolf game where courses are made up of many connected phone screens. This started as a Hackathon project in 2024 at HackTrinity in Dublin. I decided to rebuild and continue it at home, and it's still up and running. The domain name is quite cool (literally 'multi.golf'. Yes, '.golf' is a valid TLD). It was a LOT of work.

name: TicTacToe Video
description: An interactive YouTube video that you can play TicTacToe against by going to certain timestamps in the video to make your moves. It's quite cool.

name: Numcodes
description: Are humans capable of thinking of truly random numbers? I don't think so. I trained a pattern-finding statistical model ('AI') to determine if a number you entered is actually random or you just typed in random digits. Try generating 'truly' random numbers using dice, Google or any other semi-random generator and trying those out. Can my model detect when you think of them vs when they're generated?

name: Airplane Game
description: I made a simple JS web game and shared the creation on YouTube for a younger audience. I was fresh out of high school and decided that day to make a YouTube video and upload it to the internet, showing my face. It was a decision I made long ago. In a way, this was the 'real' starting point of my YouTube channel. The material is in German. The game should still be playable even if you don't speak German.

name: Norsecode
description: I thought I could teach myself to read messages by making my phone buzz the message in morse code in my pocket. I also optimized my own version of morse code. Surprisingly, this won me the regional round of the science competition 'Jugend Forscht' in the state of Lower Saxony in 2023. Looking back at it, this project had a weird 'vibe', but I somehow argued that this was in fact 'creating a new human sense', which was, needless to say, overselling it a bit.

name: Terml
description: I thought I'd make my own programming website for my terminal website to run on in the future. Turns out I was really bad at making a programming language. But it's so fun! You should read the examples on the GitHub Repo; it's quite funky.

name: teleasy
description: I got so frustrated trying to make telegram bots using the public python libraries that I made my own library. If this was still maintained, it would actually be a cool library, since it's really easy to use! Yes, it's even on PyPi (who knows for how long, it's not maintained after all).

name: Miniwelt
description: A voxel game which lets you build and easily share 256x256x256 worlds. You can change the scale of the player with a push of the button, which means that things get crazy. It's a pretty complex and cool game made to be used across many devices. It even runs on your phone! It's hosted on Cloudflare and has accounts, moderation and a bunch of fun worlds. Unfortunately, it has no users (though I might make a YouTube video about it some day).

name: Mercator
description: A website visualization of how different cylindrical map projections work. There might be a video coming about this some day.

name: Bad Captchas
description: I wanted to make a YouTube video about funny and stupid ideas of CAPTCHAs that I would implement for people to try and pass. I never actually made the video, but some ideas got implemented.

name: Bad JS Chess Engine
description: Not much to say about it. It's just a bad chess engine. I also made a version where you can play against your friends. Castling and En Passant are implemented incorrectly I believe. But you can still try to beat my engine; it's probably rated at about 1100 Elo.

name: Convert
description: This was probably my first real programming website project. It's a tool which lets you write a program in an abstract Scratch-like language and then lets you 'compile' that program into multiple programming languages. I think the idea was quite cool!

name: Coville Game
description: This was an attempt to turn my Covid in Coville project into a game where you are in the seat of a local government and are supposed to try to mitigate an epidemic spreading through town. The game never got finished, but the concept and demo are quite cool.

name: Draw
description: A website that lets you draw on an infinitely extendable surface. Useful to doodle sometimes. Really, really simple.

name: Digital Escape Rooms
description: During Covid, I came up with the great idea to create online Escape Rooms that teams can work in. This website contains some fun puzzles that people were supposed to solve together. I made some other digital escape rooms but lost the files unfortunately. They were played by my parents. Later, I joined a theatre play whose theme was being stuck in an escape room together. I like to think that this somehow inspired that play.

name: Image Crop
description: A friend asked me to make a simple website where you can crop images to A4 and other weird aspect ratios, so I made it for him (at the time, I didn't know how scandalous A4 would be).

name: AI Name Generator
description: A friend of mine wanted to find a new name for themselves. I made this website that uses the power of 'AI' (a tiny neural net that doesn't work at all) to find you a name. You first rate a couple of names from 1 to 10. Then, you let a network I coded myself train on your ratings and then let the network rate all names in the database to find the one you enjoy most. Unfortunately, it doesn't work very well. But it is fun!

name: Pangram Search
description: I tried finding a good German perfect pangram (a sentence containing every letter exactly once). I found a good candidate and made a fun YouTube video about it too. The video is in German. I also made a fun website which helps to find them. The German language makes it much easier than English, since you have additional vowels in the form of Umlaute (äöü), which help massively when constructing words and especially sensical sentences.

name: Library of Papel
description: I decided to make a digital art gallery showing all the proof pictures from the paper packing project. If you want to understand what these mean, you should read the research paper. The library code is a copy of the Library of Léon project.

name: Webcam Games
description: I always liked the idea of consoles like the Nintendo Wii or the XBOX Kinect things where you could actually move in real life to interact with the games. So I made two games which let you interact with the real world through the webcam.

name: Random Number Websites
description: My physics teacher in high school used to pick students at random to present the homework. So I made him a website which gives a random number. In fact I made two. Allegations arose that I somehow manipulated the results, but no one ever managed to prove anything.

name: Real-Life Random Walk
description: I decided to do a random walk in Zürich, by rolling a dice at every intersection and walking in that direction for 10 hours. I made a YouTube video about it and a lot of simulations. I think the video turned out great.

name: Struktogramm Editor
description: A website to create Struktogramms, which are a type of pseudocode diagram used to describe code flow. The cool thing about the website is that you can even run the code, effectively interpreting the diagram as JS code.

name: Tenmin
description: I thought it would be fun to test my sense of time by having to click a button every minute. It's fun to do regularly and see if you improve.

name: Walk to Trinity
description: Every weekday, a friend and I organised a walk to college from Trinity Halls to Trinity College in Dublin. The walk was approximately 5 kilometers and a few people showed up. We even had a leaderboard!

name: Wurzle
description: A daily game about finding a root of a hidden function. Description from the website: 'There is a secret function behind the scenes and you need to find a root (i.e. an x where f(x)=0). You can input x values and you will be shown corresponding outputs. If the response is (approximately) zero, you win! The fewer values you need, the better your score.'

name: Function Personality Test
description: A personality test that assigns you a mathematical function. For fun!

name: Searching Angela Merkel on Wikipedia
description: If you start at a random Wikipedia article in the German version of Wikipedia and want to go to Angela Merkel's article with the fewest clicks possible by just clicking links within the article body, how long do you take on average if you play optimally? That unnecessarily long question sparked the idea for my second ever serious YouTube video! Unfortunately, it's in German. So I'll spoil: 2.887 (surprisingly low, right??). You should learn German and watch the video!

name: Locating Max Giesinger
description: For my third ever serious YouTube video, I tried to find the birthplace of German Singer and Songwriter Max Giesinger. In one of the most famous German songs ever, he sings (this is the beginning of the song '80 Millionen' by him): 'Da wo ich herkomm wohnen eintausend Menschen. Im Ort daneben schon zweimal so viel. 300 Tausend in der nächsten Großstadt.' This translates roughly to 'I come from a place with 1000 people. The town next to it has two times as many. 300 thousand in the next big city.' And I thought that this would be enough to determine his birthplace without looking it up. So I did the calculation and figured out a spot and even biked there. However, it turns out he just lied. He confirmed this when I texted him about it on Instagram. What a shame. The video is of course in German.

name: Crowd-Counting
description: I always asked myself how people count people at protests. In general, how does one measure how many people are in a given crowd? So I went to a few protests, counted myself and also counted with a scientist who has been doing that for the last few years. The video about it is in German.

name: Bitcoin Talk
description: I have a feature on my website that calculates friendship scores. While programming that, I accidentally programmed a bitcoin miner. If you want to know how that happened and learn something about crypto (I promise I'm not a crypto bro, it's just a good story) along the way, watch the talk I gave at ZUCCMAP at ETH Zürich in 2024!

name: Opinions on the Metaverse
description: When I was young, I played a lot of Minecraft. I think I grew up in a kind of Metaverse. And I think a lot of us did and I think some (especially older) people don't get the implications of this. So I made a video about it!

name: MrBeast Progress Bar Rewarping
description: Matt Parker made a great video about how MrBeast warped some progress bars in videos to progress non-linearly, probably to make people watch ads for longer. So I made videos where I warped the video in weird ways such that the progress bar moved linearly again. This project is the starting point of interactions with Matt Parker.

name: Loneliest Point in Germany
description: What point in Germany is furthest from any house? In other words, how far from civilisation can you get? I calculated points, traveled to the furthest one and unfortunately found something there which made me very unhappy (you can probably guess what I found). I made a video about it, especially talking about Voronoi Diagrams, which are exactly the right tool for this job.

name: Chaotic Bad Apple
description: I found a way to encode images into the Baker Map, so I made Bad Apple but on the Baker's Map. In the video, I explain what the Baker Map is, how it works and how we can encode images.
